newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: STANBIC SHARES HIT AS PEPSI BOTTLER SINKS.
newsitem.headline: STANBIC SHARES HIT AS PEPSI BOTTLER SINKS.

text.p: Standard Bank Investment Corp Ltd fell on Monday after news that local Pepsi bottler New Age Beverages (NAB) had applied for liquidation, dealers said.
A Stanbic spokesman said that its Standard Merchant Bank unit was a major creditor of NAB which filed for voluntary liquidation on Friday.
Standard Bank shares fell as far as 200 rand from a previous close of 212.75 rand, before recovering slightly to 205.25 rand.
"Stanbic is down on fears that it will have to write off millions and that is filtering through to its share price," a dealer said.
NAB is 25 percent owned by PepsiCo International and local black business owns eight percent. The rest is held by African-American investors.
NAB's application for liquidation comes just three years after it made a high-profile return to South Africa.
